record.paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
record.context_brief: Resolution and exposure for source searches
record.original_question: What event-by-event energy resolution, mass resolution, and total exposure are needed for future ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray observatories to identify individual sources while limiting spillover from lower-energy isotropic events and limiting the blurring produced by heavier, more strongly deflected primaries?

evidence.quote: Identifying individual sources of UHECR would answer that question and remains the ultimate goal of future studies.

Identifying such sources calls for a precise shower-by-shower determination of the energy and mass of the primary particle to avoid cosmic rays of lower energy diluting the event sample and to avoid heavy primaries, suffering stronger deﬂections, blurring the source spots in the sky.

Assuming all events belowEthresh being isotropic and those above being correlated to sources, 58 % of the events observed above the applied threshold would be isotropic background and dilute the signal.
However, the ﬂux of UHECRs drops at the same time by an increase of a factor of two, so that the relaxation in energy resolution from 10 % to 30 % needs to be compensated by a factor two in exposure.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a future observatory that detects ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), with each detected air shower yielding an estimate of the primary particle's energy E and mass number A. Suppose the true differential flux dN/dE follows a steeply falling spectrum (with a suppression above roughly 4×10^19 eV), and that events with true energy below a threshold E_thresh are isotropically distributed on the celestial sphere, while events with true energy above E_thresh are clustered around a discrete set of astrophysical point sources. Reconstructed energies are subject to a Gaussian (or similar) event-by-event energy resolution σ_E/E, and reconstructed mass numbers are subject to a mass resolution σ_lnA. Heavier primaries are deflected by intervening magnetic fields by an angle proportional to their charge Z, broadening the apparent source spots.

Determine quantitative requirements on (i) the event-by-event energy resolution σ_E/E, (ii) the event-by-event mass resolution σ_lnA, and (iii) the total integrated exposure (in km² sr yr) such that, after applying energy and mass cuts above E_thresh, the resulting sample (a) contains less than a specified fraction f_bg of isotropic spillover events from the steeply falling sub-threshold population that pass cuts due to finite energy resolution, and (b) localizes individual point sources to within a specified angular scale despite magnetic deflections of heavier primaries, while retaining enough events above threshold to detect the sources at a prescribed statistical significance.

In particular, quantify how relaxing the energy resolution from 10% to 30% must be compensated by an increase in exposure given the steepness of the spectrum, and identify the minimum mass-resolution requirement that suppresses heavy-primary blurring of source images.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a forward-looking design question for next-generation UHECR observatories (e.g., AugerPrime, GCOS, POEMMA). No definitive set of resolution and exposure requirements has been universally established; design studies are ongoing and the goal of identifying individual UHECR sources has not yet been achieved.

status_evidence.title: GCOS - The Global Cosmic Ray Observatory
status_evidence.snippet: GCOS aims at unprecedented exposure and per-event mass/energy resolution to identify individual UHECR sources; design parameters are still under study.
status_evidence.claim: Requirements remain under active investigation; no settled answer.
